answer_raw:
**MLX is faster for raw throughput**, but **Ollama is the better choice for agent-based workflows**.

The performance gap depends entirely on your use case. If you are running benchmarks or validating models, **MLX** is faster; for instance, on an M4 Max, MLX can run a 35B-A3B model at roughly twice the speed of Ollama, hitting 60-70+ tok/s compared to ~35 tok/s via Ollama [4]. However, for AI agents like Claude Code, **Ollama** is the standard as it serves as the host for the agent path, while MLX is used for overnight benchmarks [1].

Regarding the biggest model you can run on 48 GB of unified memory:

**The 70B model class is your realistic ceiling with quantization.**
With 48 GB of unified memory, you can run **30B models at full precision** or load **70B models using Q4 quantization** [3]. While a 48 GB machine is comfortable up to about a 30 GB model on disk, you can technically run larger models by using quantization or swapping to disk [8]. For 70B models, the M4 Pro's 273 GB/s bandwidth makes them usable, though they may be slower than they would be on a higher-bandwidth machine like an M3 Max [5][6].
